research_question: Can a project-scoped, revision-aware, human-readable offline evidence handover command justify payment versus free Obsidian/Joplin workflows?

competitive_evidence.name: Obsidian Project Versioning community plugin
competitive_evidence.source_type: open-source repository README; developer claims, not independently installed
features_claimed: Line-level diff and Markdown/JSON audit reports
Export selected snapshots without overwriting existing files
competitive_evidence.overlap: Project-level versioned archive, diff report and export overlap heavily with the proposed evidence handover workflow.
competitive_evidence.limitations: README says community-directory installation is pending acceptance; manual installation may be required. Adoption, Windows reliability and user demand not independently verified.
competitive_evidence.competitive_implication: Do not claim project snapshots, diff reports or offline export are unique paid features.

competitive_evidence.name: Obsidian Export Studio community plugin
competitive_evidence.source_type: Obsidian community plugin listing; developer claims, not independently installed
features_claimed: Selected notes and linked notes to PDF or HTML
Cover page, table of contents, page numbers
Export does not overwrite existing files
competitive_evidence.overlap: A readable one-command handover bundle is not automatically a unique feature; a free core app plus plugin can export a structured collection.
competitive_evidence.limitations: No verified export of historical note revisions; plugin installation and cross-plugin interoperability not tested.
competitive_evidence.competitive_implication: Compare a real revision-inclusive handover workflow against this plugin before claiming a paid advantage.

competitive_evidence.name: Obsidian built-in File Recovery
competitive_evidence.overlap: Basic note versioning, before/after comparison and restore already exist in a free core product.
competitive_evidence.competitive_implication: Version history alone cannot justify payment.

competitive_evidence.name: Joplin desktop note history
competitive_evidence.overlap: Free desktop note revisions and restore already exist.
competitive_evidence.competitive_implication: Only an independently demonstrated workflow advantage, not generic revisions, could differentiate.

competitive_evidence.name: Joplin Backup plugin
features_claimed: JEX backup excludes note revision history
competitive_evidence.overlap: Revision-inclusive portable handover remains a possible gap in this specific JEX backup route.
competitive_evidence.limitations: This does not prove that other Joplin plugins or manual workflows cannot export revisions.
competitive_evidence.competitive_implication: A possible gap, not a verified unique feature or willingness-to-pay.

competitive_evidence.name: Mini Diarium
competitive_evidence.source_type: official vendor page; not independently installed
competitive_evidence.overlap: Offline journal, privacy, backup and readable export are already available for free.
competitive_evidence.competitive_implication: Do not claim offline, privacy, or export alone as a paid differentiator.

candidate_distinctions.idea: Explicit human-entered event/reason per note revision and project timeline
candidate_distinctions.required_test: Compare a complete event-log task against Obsidian Project Versioning, templates and Joplin plugins; measure steps and time with five target users.

candidate_distinctions.idea: Revision-inclusive handover containing selected historical versions, reason trail and a readable summary in one offline package
candidate_distinctions.required_test: Export the same example project with Obsidian Export Studio plus Project Versioning and Joplin history/backup, and compare recipient usability and completeness.

not_paid_differentiators: project snapshots and diff reports alone
buyer_persona_hypothesis: Windows field auditor or restricted-network project handover operator; no verified interviews
price_hypothesis: JPY 500–1200 one-time only if paid willingness-to-pay is directly validated

validation_protocol.stage_1: Collect 10 dated, direct Microsoft Store review links, recording actual complaints and purchase status when shown; do not fabricate review counts.
validation_protocol.stage_2: Interview 5 target users, first asking them to perform an evidence handover using their current free workflow and documenting time/errors.
validation_protocol.stage_3: Create only a noncommercial 1024x768 JA/EN clickable prototype of event reasons plus revision-inclusive export; no Store packaging.
validation_protocol.stage_4: Blind compare recipient comprehension and task completion against Obsidian/Joplin free workflows; document two demonstrated advantages and a solved complaint.
validation_protocol.stage_5: Ask users whether they would pay the proposed one-time price, then independently rescore all seven market-fit dimensions; never auto-promote.

gate.identity_status: REFERENCE_AVAILABLE; no repeat request; source/request binding remains separately gated

limitations: Desk review only. No independent competitor installations, plugin combinations, Store review extraction, interviews, usability trials, or real Windows GUI QA. Feature claims from third-party README/listings are not audited.
